fix_audit.notes: B1, B2, B3, W1, W2, W5, W6(partial), W7, W9, W10, W11, W12, N1-N7, N12, N14-N17 verified fixed in the worktree.

findings.title: Failure paths ignore taken_over_at: a bounce/wrong-person on a landlord-handled row re-enters the correction loop or exhausts it, killing the §8.6 late-completion transition and dead-ending the row
findings.location: server/src/reference_checks/sql/find_reference_call_by_send_ref.sql (WHERE status IN queued/contact_initiated, no taken_over_at); mark_awaiting_correction.sql:17-20; exhaust_reference_call.sql:29-30; complete_reference_call.sql (WHERE status='contact_initiated')
findings.evidence: find_reference_call_by_send_ref.sql: 'WHERE rc.status IN (\'queued\', \'contact_initiated\')' — no taken_over_at filter; mark_awaiting_correction.sql: 'WHERE id = $1 AND status IN (\'queued\', \'contact_initiated\')' — no taken_over_at; exhaust_reference_call.sql: 'WHERE id = $1 AND status IN (\'queued\', \'contact_initiated\')' — no taken_over_at; complete_reference_call.sql: 'WHERE id = $1 AND status = \'contact_initiated\''
findings.detail: Take-over writes only taken_over_at (status sticks), so a taken-over row stays queued/contact_initiated and matches the delivery-failure find. A redelivered pre-take-over bounce then yanks it to awaiting_correction (or, at correction_cycles>=1, exhausts it to unreachable + stamps referee_contact_invalid). The landlord's correction re-queues it queued+taken_over+token cleared — the sweep excludes taken-over rows forever, so the corrected contact is never re-invited and the form link is dead: permanent dead-end. The §8.6 promise ('a late form completion still transitions') is broken because complete_reference_call requires contact_initiated.
findings.recommended_fix: Add AND taken_over_at IS NULL to find_reference_call_by_send_ref (and the wrong-person route's status guard), or stand down in apply_delivery_failure/apply_wrong_person when the matched row is taken over; pin with a taken-over-row bounce test.

findings.title: STILL PRESENT (r1 W3): stale-bounce gate is format-mixed — same-day redelivered pre-correction bounces still exhaust the corrected row and fabricate referee_contact_invalid
findings.evidence: webhooks.gleam: 'let genuine_failure = case row.matched_send_at { "" -> True; at -> case row.corrected_at { "" -> True; corrected -> string.compare(at, corrected) != order.Lt } }' — at is RFC3339 (sweep now_iso()/to_rfc3339: '2026-08-12T08:00:00Z'), corrected is Postgres ::text ('2026-08-12 08:05:00.123456+00'). 'T'(0x54) > ' '(0x20) at index 10: every same-day send compares >= the correction.
findings.detail: The comment 'ISO timestamps — lexical compare is chronological' is false across the two producers. A same-day redelivered pre-correction bounce (the common webhook-retry case) classifies as genuine and exhaust_reference_call terminalizes the corrected row as unreachable + stamps referee_contact_invalid — the exact W3 fabrication the gate was built to prevent. The pin tests only exercise cross-day fixtures (2026-08-01 vs run-date).
findings.recommended_fix: Normalize both sides to one format before comparing (e.g. compare the RFC3339 send stamp against corrected_at cast to text with to_char(...,'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS"Z"'), or compare epoch millis server-side), and pin with a SAME-DAY stale-bounce test.

findings.title: Correction clears the token but leaves form_opened_at + draft_answers live — the wrong person's draft answers rehydrate into the corrected referee's form and the co-nudge is suppressed forever
findings.evidence: correct_reference_call.sql: 'form_token = NULL, form_token_expires_at = NULL' — no form_opened_at/draft_answers clearing; form_handler.gleam:162: 'let draft = questions.decode_draft(row.draft_answers)' (the corrected referee's fresh token rehydrates the stored draft); sweep.gleam co_nudge_should_fire: '!form_was_opened(row) && !has_draft_answers(row)'
findings.detail: The §8.3 correction swaps the referee contact but the row still carries the previous person's form session: the corrected referee's fresh link rehydrates the wrong person's answers (data contamination of the reference evidence), and form_opened_at already set suppresses the A2 co-nudge for the whole corrected cycle.
findings.recommended_fix: Clear form_opened_at and draft_answers in correct_reference_call alongside the token (the B1 fix cleared the capability; the session state must die with it).

findings.title: STILL PRESENT (r1 W8): late-response guard is partial — a stale ApiReturnedRefcheckAction still toasts on unrelated pages because application_detail survives navigation and the id-match guard never checks the route
findings.location: client/src/client.gleam:3522-3559 (handler), 6584-6596 (find_refcheck_call), 651 (detail reset only on entering the detail route)
findings.evidence: find_refcheck_call: 'case model.application_detail { Success(detail) -> ... }' — the guard searches the RETAINED detail; BrowserChangedUrl sets 'application_detail: Loading' only in the 'routes.ApplicationDetail(vid, aid) ->' branch; the success arm unconditionally 'add_toast(cleared, toast_copy, ToastSuccess)'.
findings.detail: The W8 fix dropped stale responses only when the call id is absent from the retained detail; navigating detail → dashboard keeps the old detail in the model, so a late action response still pops a success toast on the dashboard (the refetch is route-guarded, the toast is not). The comment claims the guard drops late answers — it only partially does.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a route check to ApiReturnedRefcheckAction (drop unless model.route is ApplicationDetail for the same vid/aid), or clear application_detail on every non-detail navigation.

findings.title: STILL PRESENT (r1 W4): the resend path's effective() lacks the correction_cycles gate — a cleared channel falls back to the proven-dead snapshot address on the referee's expired-link resend
findings.evidence: fn effective(corrected: Option(String), snapshot: Option(String)) -> Option(String) { case corrected, snapshot { Some(c), _ -> Some(c); None, s -> s } }' — no correction_cycles input; sweep.gleam:709-732 has the corrected-only rule the resend path does not share.
findings.detail: W4's corrected-replaces-snapshot rule landed in the sweep + find fallback but not in the expired-link resend: after a correction that cleared one channel, a referee-initiated resend re-contacts the snapshot address that already failed (AD-7 never-re-contact violated — potentially messaging the wrong person).
findings.recommended_fix: Thread correction_cycles into the resend send and apply the same corrected-only rule (cleared channel = no channel).

findings.title: Substitute edit-trio prefills the terminal referee's own contact and the server accepts an identical trio — one-click re-invite of an objected/unreachable person routes around the Art 21 hard stop and the exhaustion stamp
findings.location: client/src/client.gleam:6680-6695 (prefill_refcheck_edit); client/src/components/reference_panel.gleam:1000-1011 (view_edit_trio prefill); server/src/reference_checks/sql/substitute_reference_call.sql (INSERT has no contact-difference guard)
findings.evidence: prefill_refcheck_edit: '#(reference_panel.effective_name_value(call), reference_panel.effective_email_value(call), reference_panel.effective_phone_value(call))' — the terminal row's OWN contact; substitute_reference_call.sql INSERT 'SELECT application_id, ref_slot, owner_label, $3, NULLIF($4,''), NULLIF($5,''), now() FROM guard' — no comparison against the prior row's contact.
findings.detail: §8.2 substitution is 'the landlord asks the applicant for ANOTHER referee'. The prefill + no server-side different-contact guard lets an unchanged save create a fresh invite to the person who objected (Art 21 hard stop) or to the contact the exhaustion mechanism just stamped referee_contact_invalid on — the signal is fabricated-proof only if the flow cannot re-target the same contact.
findings.recommended_fix: Require at least one contact field to differ from the substituted row (server-side), and/or do not prefill the substitute trio with the terminal row's own contact.

findings.title: Queued rows never offer 'Take over manually' although A7/AC2 include queued in the take-over set and the server hook can_take_over is True for queued rows
findings.evidence: overflow_actions: 'Queued -> [RefcheckStart, RefcheckSkip]' — no RefcheckTakeOver arm; compute_hooks_decoded: 'can_take_over: status == Queued || status == ContactInitiated || status == Unreachable'; take_over_reference_call.sql: 'AND status IN (\'queued\', \'contact_initiated\', \'unreachable\')'
findings.detail: §7.7 offers take-over 'from unreachable or any waiting state'; the server guard + hook include queued, but the client only surfaces it on contact_initiated/unreachable. A landlord cannot take over a queued row from the UI even though the server accepts it — the hook value is dead for queued rows.
findings.recommended_fix: Offer the take-over entry for queued rows in the overflow menu (or restrict the server guard/hook to the surfaced states — one contract).

findings.title: Substitute 'existing' idempotent no-op silently drops a NEW trio: re-substituting the history row with changed details returns 200 and discards the typed referee
findings.location: server/src/reference_checks/actions_handler.gleam:363-366 (how='existing' -> Ok(new_row.id), no trio write); server/src/reference_checks/sql/substitute_reference_call.sql:44-55 (any live non-terminal successor)
findings.evidence: actions_handler: '"existing" -> Ok(new_row.id)' — the typed trio is never written; substitute_reference_call.sql second SELECT: 'AND rc.status NOT IN (\'form_completed\', \'unreachable\', \'refused\', \'objected\', \'manual_recorded\', \'failed\', \'completed\', \'partial\')' — skipped/awaiting_correction successors also match.
findings.detail: The substitute affordance stays live on the terminal history row (can_substitute_referee is status-based). A landlord who re-substitutes it with corrected details gets 200 + the substituted toast while the new trio is silently discarded — the successor keeps the old contact. The idempotent contract must not swallow legitimate new input.
findings.recommended_fix: On how='existing' with a different trio, return a 409 with a 'referee already replaced' message (or update the successor); never silently drop the submitted trio.

findings.title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS
findings.evidence: P0 guards pinned (B1 double-pin incl. negative control, substitute idempotence, take-over sweep exclusion, one-cycle guard, W3 both routes at handler level); P1/P2 gaps: no authz negatives (non-owning 404, archived 422), W9 route-reset unpinned, substitute fraud stamp untested, wrong-person notification unasserted, W4 sweep-level test missing, client ?slot= wire untested.
findings.detail: All P0 load-bearing guards are pinned, but several P1/P2 behaviours shipped without tests, so the gate sits at CONCERNS (P1 80-89%, overall >=80%).
findings.recommended_fix: Add the negative-authz tests, the W9 reset pin, and the substitute-stamp assertion to lift the gate.

findings.title: STILL PRESENT (r1 N18): take-over confirm body uses 'they' not §7.7's 'he'; the §7.4 start confirm likewise uses 'them' not 'her' — verbatim guard not fully met
findings.evidence: refcheck_take_over_confirm_body: 'If they complete the form anyway, it still shows up here.' vs UX §7.7 'If he completes the form anyway, it still shows up here.'; refcheck_start_confirm: 'We\'ll email and text them the form now.' vs §7.4 'We\'ll email and text her the form now.'
findings.detail: The name interpolation fix landed (r1 N18 half), but the gender-neutral pronoun rewrites still deviate from the spec-verbatim copy in both inline confirms. Note-level per the r1 classification; the em-dash ban itself is clean.
findings.recommended_fix: Match the spec pronouns ('he'/'her') or get an explicit product ruling that gender-neutral supersedes verbatim.

findings.title: STILL PRESENT (r1 N8/N9): the PR's own spec artifacts drift from the code — item 6 omits corrected_name, item 5 claims ONE additive column while the migration ships two (corrected_name + corrected_at), the Files list names update_application_referee_trio.sql which does not exist, and the effective-contact rule documented is the pre-W4 one
findings.evidence: spec item 6: 'additive detail keys: taken_over_at, contact_name, contact_email, contact_phone, corrected_email, corrected_phone, correction_cycles' — no corrected_name; item 5: 'ONE additive column: corrected_name TEXT' — the migration adds corrected_at too; Files: 'sql/update_application_referee_trio.sql' — three per-slot files exist instead.
findings.detail: Doc-level drift: the spec enumeration, the column count, the file names, and the documented effective-contact rule no longer match the implemented code. Zero runtime impact; the migration header comment also documents the pre-W4 fallback rule.
findings.recommended_fix: Update the spec artifacts in a follow-up (they are the round's contract record).

findings.title: STILL PRESENT (r1 N10): the live-slot ON CONFLICT predicate is maintained in three SQL files (plus the migration's partial index) — byte-consistent today, drift-prone tomorrow
findings.evidence: Three files carry the identical 'ON CONFLICT (application_id, ref_slot, owner_label) WHERE status NOT IN (\'form_completed\', \'unreachable\', \'refused\', \'objected\', \'manual_recorded\', \'failed\', \'completed\', \'partial\')' predicate, mirroring the migration's partial index.
findings.detail: The predicates are byte-identical today (verified), so no drift bug exists yet; a future status-list change must be made in four places. Maintainability note carried from r1.
findings.recommended_fix: Extract the live-slot insert into one query the substitute path reuses.

findings.title: Per-slot 'Start this check now' re-arms EVERY queued row of the application — the slot filter is ignored and the re-arm also fires on the suppressed (declined) start path; the re-arm is effectively inert because queued rows are always already due
findings.evidence: rearm_queued_reference_calls.sql: 'WHERE application_id = $1 AND status = \'queued\'::reference_call_status AND taken_over_at IS NULL' — no slot filter; run_start_action calls it unconditionally after run_create_checks_slot Ok(_) — including the Ok(Suppressed) declined path.
findings.detail: The W6 fix re-arms the whole application, contradicting the trigger's own comment ('the other slot is untouched') and AC1's per-reference promise; in v1 flows queued rows are always due, so the observable impact is nil. On the declined path it returns 200 started:true with a re-arm of any stray queued rows.
findings.recommended_fix: Scope the re-arm to the requested slot (or drop it and let the sweep's own tick govern), and skip it on the Suppressed outcome.

findings.title: Single-slot refcheck_edit: a second action choice (or any action success) silently discards another row's in-progress typed trio values; Cancel resets the trio but never closes it
findings.location: client/src/model.gleam:375-376 (single Option(RefcheckEdit)); client/src/client.gleam:3454-3472, 3543-3544 (UserEditedRefcheckTrio / success clearing); client/src/components/reference_panel.gleam:960-1010 (always-open correction trio)
findings.evidence: UserChoseRefcheckAction Substitute arm: 'refcheck_edit: Some(prefill_refcheck_edit(...))' — overwrites any open edit; success arm: 'Model(..model, refcheck_edit: None, refcheck_confirm: None, ...)' — clears the OTHER row's edit; view_correction_surface renders the trio unconditionally.
findings.detail: The awaiting_correction trio is always open; typing corrections on it, then opening a substitute edit on another row (or any action completing), silently drops the typed-but-unsaved values. Recoverable by retyping, but silent data loss in the §8.3 flow.
findings.recommended_fix: Key the edit state per call (or block the second edit while one is dirty with a confirm).

findings.title: STILL PRESENT (r1 N11): a truly concurrent substitute double-submit can still return 409 instead of the documented 200 idempotent no-op
findings.evidence: The UNION ALL's second SELECT runs under the statement snapshot taken before the concurrent INSERT committed; under READ COMMITTED the 'NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM inserted)' + successor SELECT can miss the just-committed row, yielding 0 rows -> Error(NotSubstitutable) -> 409.
findings.detail: The serialized double-submit returns 200 how='existing' (pinned), but two simultaneous submits can still race to a 409. Note-level: the landlord retries and lands on the successor; no duplicate row or audit either way.
findings.recommended_fix: Accept the 409 as the race outcome and document it, or retry the successor SELECT once after a 0-row insert.

findings.title: Substitute idempotent no-op re-stamps creation fraud on the existing successor — a full overwrite that can wipe submission-time form_session in a narrow double-submit race
findings.evidence: actions_handler: 'Ok(new_id) -> { trigger.stamp_creation_fraud_for(config, app_uuid, landlord_uuid, vacancy_uuid, [new_id]) ... }' — runs for how='existing' too; stamp_creation_fraud_signals.sql: 'SET fraud_signals = $2::jsonb' — full overwrite with form_session: null.
findings.detail: The 'existing' branch is documented as a pure no-op but still recomputes and overwrites the successor's fraud_signals (plus a fresh Twilio line-type lookup). If the successor already completed a submission between the two submits, its form_session in the denormalised column is wiped (the result document keeps its own copy).
findings.recommended_fix: Skip the fraud stamp on the how='existing' path.

findings.title: STILL PRESENT (r1 N13, partial): the client's ?slot= wire format for per-row start has no test (the server 400 branch is pinned)
findings.evidence: start_check builds '?slot=' <> s — no client test asserts the URL; the server-side invalid-slot 400 is pinned.
findings.detail: The server leg is covered; the client wire format is a small gap.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a client test asserting the ?slot= query on the start request.

findings.title: Substitution creation-fraud stamping (r1 N1 fold) has no test — the successor row's fraud_signals are never asserted
findings.evidence: No assertion reads fraud_signals on the substituted successor in the substitute tests.
findings.detail: The stamp is best-effort (AD-10) but is the N1 fold's deliverable; a pin would keep it honest.
findings.recommended_fix: Assert the successor's fraud_signals are non-null after substitution.

findings.title: No authz negatives on the new action endpoints: non-owning-landlord 404 and archived-vacancy 422 are untested for take-over/correct/substitute
findings.evidence: The HTTP happy-path test passes a REAL owning landlord now (r1 N3 fixed); no test drives a foreign landlord's call id or an archived vacancy through the new arms.
findings.detail: The ownership precheck is verified present and correct; the negative legs are unexercised.
findings.recommended_fix: Add the two negative tests (foreign landlord 404; archived vacancy 422).

findings.title: Wrong-person exhaustion leg pins status + audit but not the in-app notification
findings.evidence: wrong_person_route_exhausts_corrected_row_test asserts status and audit count only; the webhook leg asserts notification_bodies.
findings.detail: The wrong-person notification path (notify_reference_correction_exhausted) is unasserted for the SSR route.
findings.recommended_fix: Assert the notification row/bodies in the wrong-person exhaustion test.

findings.title: W4 effective-contact rule (cleared channel stays absent after correction) has no sweep-level test, and the W9 route-change reset has no pin
findings.evidence: No sweep test drives a corrected row with one cleared channel; no client test navigates away and asserts refcheck_confirm/edit/menu are None.
findings.detail: Both fixes are verified present in code; the pins are missing.
findings.recommended_fix: Add the two tests.

findings.title: Take-over confirm renders the referee's name twice (the §7.7 body already interpolates it; a caption line repeats it)
findings.evidence: view_take_over_confirm renders 'html.text(copy.refcheck_take_over_confirm_body(name))' AND 'html.text(name)' as a separate line.
findings.detail: Redundant duplicate name line inside the inline confirm; cosmetic.
findings.recommended_fix: Drop the extra caption line (or replace it with the §7.7 contact chips the spec actually promises post-confirm).

findings.title: Overflow menu declares role=menu/menuitem but has no keyboard contract — no Escape-to-close, no arrow-key navigation
findings.evidence: The menu div carries role/aria attributes and buttons; no keydown handling for Escape/arrows exists on the menu container.
findings.detail: Mouse + Tab operate the menu, but a declared menu without the WAI-ARIA keyboard contract is an a11y gap for keyboard users.
findings.recommended_fix: Add Escape-to-close and arrow navigation (or drop the menu roles).

findings.title: update_trio's unknown-slot arm fabricates a bogus pog.UnexpectedArgumentCount error (unreachable — ref_slot comes from the DB enum)
findings.evidence: '_ -> Error(pog.UnexpectedArgumentCount(expected: 5, got: 0))' — a squirrel-query-shaped error for a slot value that cannot occur.
findings.detail: Unreachable in practice; if it ever fired it would surface as a misleading 500 about query arity.
findings.recommended_fix: Use a plain Error/assert-style arm (or log-and-error) that names the slot.

findings.evidence: The trio UPDATE's WHERE is (application_id, vacancy_id) — the app is proven present by verify_application_in_vacancy precheck, and correct/substitute succeed only after their guarded row UPDATE within the same transaction (FK ensures the app row exists). 0 rows is unreachable short of a same-transaction app delete, which nothing performs.
findings.detail: The silent-0-row pattern W10 fixed is not reachable here. False positive.
findings.recommended_fix: N/A
